Comment: Retrain loop: train -> evaluate on the frozen golden set -> gate -> register PendingManualApproval -> notify. The state machine NEVER deploys. Registration is where it stops; a human approving that registry version is what emits the EventBridge event that triggers the M2 canary deploy. That separation is the whole point — an automated path from 'metrics improved' to 'serving production traffic' is the failure this design exists to prevent.

RecordTrigger.Comment: Capture WHY this retrain started. A retrain triggered by a drift breach and one triggered by a human clicking the manual workflow have different evidentiary weight later, and 'why did version 7 exist' is the first question asked when a model misbehaves.

Train.Comment: SageMaker training job, run synchronously. Trains on the training split PLUS the human corrections accumulated since the last run — which is exactly the data whose sampling bias the README discusses at length: reviewers only ever see low-confidence documents.

Retry.Comment: ResourceLimitExceeded means the account is at its instance quota — a transient condition that clears as other jobs finish, so it is worth waiting minutes rather than failing the retrain.

Evaluate.Comment: Processing job scoring the candidate on the FROZEN golden set, using the same evaluate.py that produced the champion's numbers. Deliberately not a separate evaluation path: a gate that compares numbers produced by two different code paths is comparing two different things. The job also asserts train/golden non-overlap and fails if the golden set has leaked.

ReadGateDecision.Comment: Read the gate verdict computed by evaluate.py and written into metrics.json. The gate logic lives in ONE place — the same function M1 uses — rather than being re-expressed as Choice states here. Re-implementing the comparison in ASL would mean two definitions of 'better' that can drift apart, and the one that actually blocks a release would be the one nobody tested.

Gate.Comment: THE GATE. Two independent conditions, both computed by evaluate.evaluate_gate: the candidate must beat the champion by GATE_MIN_MACRO_F1_IMPROVEMENT on the golden set, AND no single class may fall below GATE_MIN_PER_CLASS_F1. The margin exists so the gate does not fire on evaluation noise; the per-class floor exists because an overall gain can hide one collapsed class, and a model that improved on average while becoming useless for id_document must not ship.

NotifyGateFailed.Comment: The candidate did not beat the champion. Terminal SUCCESS, not failure: the gate working is the system functioning correctly, and marking it as a failed execution would put a permanent error rate on the retrain state machine and train people to ignore it. The champion stays live.

Parameters.Subject: Retrain candidate REJECTED by the gate
Parameters.Message.$: States.Format('A retrain candidate failed the promotion gate and was NOT registered. Reason: {}. Champion macro-F1: {}. Candidate macro-F1: {}. Trigger: {}. The current champion remains live; no action is required.', $.gate_input.metrics.gate.reason, $.gate_input.metrics.gate.champion_macro_f1, $.gate_input.metrics.gate.candidate_macro_f1, $.trigger.source)

RejectedByGate.Comment: Terminal success. The gate did its job.

RegisterCandidate.Comment: Register the candidate as a new Model Package version with ModelApprovalStatus = PendingManualApproval. Hardcoded here, not parameterised: the approval status is the safety property this entire milestone rests on, and making it an input would let a caller pass 'Approved' and self-deploy.

Parameters.ModelPackageDescription.$: States.Format('Retrain candidate. macro-F1 {} vs champion {}. Trigger: {} ({}).', $.gate_input.metrics.macro_f1, $.gate_input.metrics.gate.champion_macro_f1, $.trigger.source, $.trigger.verdict)

NotifyAwaitingApproval.Comment: Tell a human there is something to review. This is where the automated path ENDS. Nothing downstream of here runs until a person approves the registry version, and that approval — not this state machine — emits the EventBridge event that starts the canary deploy.

Parameters.Subject: Retrain candidate AWAITING APPROVAL

Catch.Comment: The version is registered whether or not the notification lands, so a failed publish must not fail the execution — it would look like the retrain failed when a candidate is in fact waiting.

AwaitingHumanApproval.Comment: Terminal. The candidate is registered and waiting for a human. There is deliberately no .waitForTaskToken here: approval happens in the SageMaker Model Registry console, on its own timescale, and is observed via EventBridge. Holding an execution open for days waiting on a console click would couple the retrain's lifetime to a human's calendar for no benefit.

NotifyFailure.Comment: Something in the retrain pipeline broke. Distinct from a gate rejection, which is not a failure — conflating the two would mean nobody could tell 'the model did not improve' from 'the training job crashed'.

Parameters.Subject: Retrain pipeline FAILED

RetrainFailed.Cause: The retrain pipeline failed before a gate decision could be made. See the SNS notification and the execution history.
